## Dimensions

### dim_date

A dense, gapless calendar generated from the observed fact range and padded to whole years. Gapless is the point: a missing day silently drops facts from every time-series join, so it is asserted rather than assumed.

- **Layer:** Dimension
- **Grain:** One row per calendar day, plus one Unknown member.
- **Rows:** 1,828

| Column | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `date_key` | `INTEGER` | Primary key. YYYYMMDD as an integer - readable in a result, sorts chronologically, survives a reload. -1 is the Unknown member. |
| `full_date` | `DATE` | The calendar date. NULL only on the Unknown member. |
| `calendar_year` | `BIGINT` | Four-digit calendar year. |
| `calendar_quarter` | `BIGINT` | Calendar quarter, 1-4. |
| `quarter_label` | `VARCHAR` | Quarter as a display label, e.g. 2022-Q1. |
| `calendar_month` | `BIGINT` | Calendar month, 1-12. |
| `month_name` | `VARCHAR` | Full month name, e.g. January. |
| `year_month` | `VARCHAR` | Month as YYYY-MM - the join key the monthly mart groups on. |
| `month_start_date` | `DATE` | First day of the month, for time-axis plotting. |
| `iso_year` | `BIGINT` | ISO-8601 week-numbering year, which can differ from calendar_year at a year boundary. |
| `iso_week` | `BIGINT` | ISO-8601 week number, 1-53. |
| `iso_week_label` | `VARCHAR` | ISO year and week as a display label, e.g. 2022-W03. |
| `week_start_date` | `DATE` | Monday of the ISO week. |
| `day_of_month` | `BIGINT` | Day of the month, 1-31. |
| `iso_day_of_week` | `BIGINT` | ISO day of week, 1 = Monday through 7 = Sunday. |
| `day_name` | `VARCHAR` | Full day name, e.g. Tuesday. |
| `is_weekend` | `BOOLEAN` | True on Saturday and Sunday. Reporting often thins at weekends, so this is worth having when reading gaps. |
| `is_month_end` | `BOOLEAN` | True on the last calendar day of the month. |

### dim_indicator

Parsed out of the publisher's free-text indicator labels by pipelines/stage.py::parse_indicator. The attribute that matters most is is_additive_over_time, which records whether a measure may be summed across dates.

- **Layer:** Dimension
- **Grain:** One row per real-world measure, plus one Unknown member. The unit variant is pivoted onto the fact, not carried here.
- **Rows:** 5

| Column | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `indicator_key` | `INTEGER` | Surrogate primary key. -1 is the Unknown member. |
| `indicator_code` | `VARCHAR` | Stable snake_case natural key, e.g. daily_intensive_care_occupancy. |
| `indicator_name` | `VARCHAR` | Human-readable measure name. |
| `care_setting` | `VARCHAR` | Intensive care or All hospital. |
| `metric_type` | `VARCHAR` | Occupancy or New admissions. |
| `reporting_frequency` | `VARCHAR` | Daily or Weekly, as published. |
| `measure_semantics` | `VARCHAR` | Stock (point-in-time) or Flow (period total). |
| `is_additive_over_time` | `BOOLEAN` | True when the measure may be summed across dates. Occupancy is a stock, so summing it counts the same patient once per night; admissions are a flow and may be summed. |
| `default_time_aggregation` | `VARCHAR` | The aggregate function that matches the semantics - 'sum' for flows, 'avg' for stocks. |
| `source_count_label` | `VARCHAR` | The publisher's original label for the absolute-count variant, kept for traceability. |
| `source_rate_label` | `VARCHAR` | The publisher's original label for the per-million variant. |

### dim_location

The conformed geography dimension, assembled from ISO 3166-1 plus a hand-maintained override file for the publisher codes that are not ISO. It deliberately covers the full ISO country list rather than only the ~50 locations that report activity: a conformed dimension describes the domain, the facts describe what was measured.

- **Layer:** Dimension
- **Grain:** One row per reporting location, plus one Unknown member.
- **Rows:** 254

| Column | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `location_key` | `INTEGER` | Surrogate primary key, assigned by row_number() over the natural key. -1 is the Unknown member. |
| `source_location_code` | `VARCHAR` | Natural key - the publisher's own code. An ISO alpha-3 for countries, an OWID_* pseudo-code for the four UK nations. |
| `location_name` | `VARCHAR` | Display name of the location. |
| `iso_alpha_2` | `VARCHAR` | ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code. NULL for non-ISO locations. |
| `iso_alpha_3` | `VARCHAR` | ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 code. NULL for non-ISO locations. |
| `location_type` | `VARCHAR` | Country or Sub-national. Sub-national rows exist because Our World in Data reports England, Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland separately. |
| `parent_iso_alpha_3` | `VARCHAR` | For a sub-national location, the country it belongs to (GBR for the UK nations). Equals iso_alpha_3 for countries. |
| `region` | `VARCHAR` | UN M49 region, e.g. Europe. Never NULL for a location that reports activity - that is asserted. |
| `sub_region` | `VARCHAR` | UN M49 sub-region, e.g. Northern Europe. |
| `intermediate_region` | `VARCHAR` | UN M49 intermediate region where one exists, otherwise 'Not applicable'. |
| `has_population_data` | `BOOLEAN` | True when a World Bank population series exists. False means population-derived rates are left NULL rather than guessed. |
| `reports_hospital_activity` | `BOOLEAN` | True when this location appears in the fact table. Separates the domain from what was actually measured. |
| `classification_source` | `VARCHAR` | Where the classification came from - 'ISO 3166-1' or 'config/location_overrides.csv'. Makes the hand-maintained rows auditable. |

## Facts

### fct_hospital_activity

The centre of the star: daily and weekly hospital and ICU activity, with the publisher's rate, an independently derived rate, and the difference between them kept as a measure.

- **Layer:** Fact
- **Grain:** One row per location, date and indicator. Enforced by fct_activity_grain_is_unique.
- **Rows:** 115,262

| Column | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `date_key` | `INTEGER` | Foreign key to dim_date. |
| `location_key` | `INTEGER` | Foreign key to dim_location. |
| `indicator_key` | `INTEGER` | Foreign key to dim_indicator. |
| `event_date` | `DATE` | The observation date, carried on the fact so it can be filtered without a join. |
| `reported_value` | `DOUBLE` | The publisher's absolute count - beds occupied, or admissions in the period. |
| `reported_per_million` | `DOUBLE` | The publisher's own population-adjusted rate. |
| `reported_per_100k` | `DOUBLE` | The publisher's rate rescaled to per 100,000. THE measure to compare across locations: the publisher's denominator matches the geography its numerator covers. |
| `population` | `BIGINT` | This location's population in the calendar year of the observation, carried onto the fact so every rate below is reproducible from the row alone. NULL where no series exists. |
| `derived_per_million` | `DOUBLE` | Rate recomputed here from reported_value and population. An independent control, not the headline number. |
| `derived_per_100k` | `DOUBLE` | The same control at the per-100,000 scale. |
| `rate_variance_pct` | `DOUBLE` | Signed percentage difference between the derived and the published rate. The reconciliation measure: near zero almost everywhere, ~-7% for Poland (census vintage), ~-32% for Cyprus (the two sources cover different populations). |
| `is_statistical_outlier` | `BOOLEAN` | Flagged by a median/MAD modified z-score within the series. A review flag, never a filter - epidemic curves are legitimately spiky. |
| `is_population_unknown` | `BOOLEAN` | True where no population was available, so the derived rates are NULL by design rather than by accident. |
| `warehouse_built_at` | `TIMESTAMP` | When this row's model was last built. Cheap lineage on every row. |

### fct_population_annual

A periodic snapshot fact. Population is modelled as a fact rather than an attribute on dim_location because it is a measured quantity that changes every year - putting it on the dimension would either freeze it or force a slowly-changing dimension for what is simply a yearly measurement. World Bank aggregates ("World", "OECD members", the income groups) are excluded upstream so nothing here can double-count a population.

- **Layer:** Fact
- **Grain:** One row per location and calendar year.
- **Rows:** 13,945

| Column | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `location_key` | `INTEGER` | Foreign key to dim_location. |
| `calendar_year` | `INTEGER` | The year the estimate refers to. |
| `population` | `BIGINT` | Mid-year population estimate. Semi-additive: additive across locations, never across years. |
| `population_millions` | `DOUBLE` | population / 1e6, for readability in ad-hoc queries. |
| `source_location_code` | `VARCHAR` | The ISO alpha-3 the row was joined on, kept for traceability. |

## Reporting marts

### mart_location_coverage

How complete each series is. Reporting gaps are the failure mode that quietly corrupts cross-country comparison, so completeness is measured inside each location's own reporting span and graded against the indicator's own cadence (a weekly series legitimately reports one day in seven).

- **Layer:** Reporting mart
- **Grain:** One row per location and indicator.
- **Rows:** 139

| `reporting_completeness_pct` | `DOUBLE` |
| `days_behind_dataset` | `BIGINT` |
| `rows_without_population` | `HUGEINT` |
| `coverage_grade` | `VARCHAR` |

### mart_monthly_activity

Monthly rollup, aggregated according to each measure's own semantics: stocks get avg and max, flows get sum. monthly_value and monthly_per_100k carry whichever aggregation the indicator declares, so a chart can plot any measure without knowing the difference.

### mart_rate_reconciliation

The assurance mart. Compares the publisher's rate against the derived one and grades the result, back-solving the denominator the publisher must have used so a mismatch is diagnosable rather than merely visible.

- **Layer:** Reporting mart
- **Grain:** One row per location and indicator.
- **Rows:** 127

| `indicator_name` | `VARCHAR` |
| `rows_compared` | `BIGINT` |
| `mean_variance_pct` | `DOUBLE` |
